policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Read the required quantities and colors from the goal at every step; unrequested colors have quota zero. First update the deposit counters from the observed execution interval. All supplied episodes start in A with an empty hand and counters zero. Apply these rules to the current situation rather than advancing a stored phase: if all requested quotas are satisfied, choose C, press the button, even if more cubes remain visible. Otherwise, if a requested cube is currently held, choose B, put it into the bin. A successful A therefore leads to B; a completed B leads to C if the updated counters meet every quota, and otherwise to A. If the hand is empty and a quota remains, choose A targeting a visible free cube of a still-needed color. For mixed-color goals, use the matching goal-and-layout preference below to choose which needed color to finish first; do not apply a universal green-first rule. All preference indices use the updated deposit counters after processing the current execution interval. The instruction does not specify an ordering among same-color cubes; to reproduce the supplied choices use these scene-conditioned tie-breaks, matching approximate locations to current visible objects rather than requiring exact pixel equality: for two blue cubes with the bin near [123, 141], select the cube near [86, 136] when blue_deposited is zero and near [86, 88] when it is one. For three red cubes with the bin near [110, 130], select near [67, 157], [115, 189], or [71, 137] when red_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For three blue cubes with the bin near [91, 111], select near [96, 82], [67, 115], or [117, 106] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For the mixed goal with the bin near [130, 117], select green near [80, 91], [105, 116], or [106, 162] when green_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two; after three green deposits select red near [63, 84]. For the one-green goal select the initially visible green cube near [81, 153]. For three blue and two green with the bin near [90, 148], finish green first: select green near [99, 82] or [118, 81] when green_deposited is respectively zero or one, then blue near [61, 171], [112, 152], or [88, 184] when blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For one red with the bin near [112, 177], select red near [79, 127]. For two red and three green with the bin near [94, 155], finish green first: select green near [68, 178], [71, 75], or [90, 181] when green_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two, then red near [54, 99] or [100, 121] when red_deposited is respectively zero or one. For two blue with the bin near [122, 181], select blue near [91, 163] or [97, 117] when blue_deposited is respectively zero or one. For two red and one green with the bin near [107, 86], finish red first: select red near [74, 98] or [64, 83] when red_deposited is respectively zero or one, then green near [105, 117]. For three blue with the bin near [105, 100], select blue near [64, 75], [94, 138], or [54, 118] when updated blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. For one red and one green with the bin near [101, 173], finish red first, selecting red near [86, 69], then green near [96, 104]. For one red with the bin near [117, 169] and a red arrangement including cubes near [56, 177], [98, 84], [110, 112], [111, 65], and [117, 82], select red near [98, 84]. For three blue and two green with the bin near [101, 141], finish blue first: select blue near [54, 104], [71, 130], or [64, 80] when updated blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two; after three blue deposits select green near [101, 176] or [52, 122] when updated green_deposited is respectively zero or one. These preferences apply only to approximately matching goals and layouts and select currently observed cubes, not fixed points independent of the scene. Match a layout using the goal, bin, and visible cube arrangement together, never bin proximity alone. Compare the remaining visible candidates with the preference's remaining candidates using updated counters; already deposited cubes need not remain visible. This joint matching distinguishes nearby-bin layouts with different target choices or color orders. Apply a matching preference before the smallest-y-then-smallest-x fallback. Output A's point within the selected cube, in [y, x] order, using its current visible position. B and C need no point. For an unfamiliar layout or absent preferred candidate, choose another visible free cube of a needed color, breaking ties by smallest y then smallest x. A failed grasp with an empty hand leads to another A, without incrementing any counter. If a needed cube is temporarily occluded, use its latest clearly observed location in the current interval. If no needed candidate is observable anywhere in that interval, make a best-effort A at the most plausible accessible location rather than falsely declaring completion; preserve counters unless a deposit is actually observed.

fields.name: blue_deposited
fields.description: Initialize to zero if incoming memory is empty. Otherwise start from the incoming integer. Recognize a completed blue deposit from the combined execution-interval evidence: a blue cube is held during transport toward the bin's elevated release pose, the fingers open there, and the gripper withdraws empty, with no observed evidence that the carried cube fell outside the bin. Direct visibility of entry into the opaque bin is not required. Do not identify a remaining nearby blue cube as the released cube solely by image proximity; use its earlier presence and the carried cube's motion within this interval to distinguish them. Increment once per such completed deposit in this interval. Use the held cube's color before release; do not count pickup, issuing B, repeated post-release frames, or unrelated cubes appearing or disappearing. Elevated wrist coordinates need not equal the bin's visible center. Preserve if no blue deposit is observed. e.g. 1
